intent.raw_query: Vietnam on $800, backpacking 10 days, street food and culture, April 2026

experiences.name: Hanoi Old Quarter Street Food Tour
experiences.description: Wander through the maze-like streets of Hanoi's Old Quarter sampling iconic Vietnamese dishes including Bun Cha, Banh Mi, Pho, and Egg Coffee from local vendors and hole-in-the-wall eateries. Join a budget walking food tour or explore independently using a street food map.

experiences.name: Hoi An Ancient Town Lantern Festival & Night Market
experiences.description: Explore the UNESCO-listed Ancient Town of Hoi An, browse the vibrant night market, and experience the magical monthly lantern festival where hundreds of silk lanterns illuminate the Thu Bon River. Try local specialties like Cao Lau and White Rose dumplings from street stalls for just a few dollars.

experiences.name: Motorbiking the Hai Van Pass
experiences.description: Rent a motorbike or join a budget group tour to ride the legendary Hai Van Pass, one of Southeast Asia's most scenic coastal mountain roads connecting Da Nang and Hue. Stop at the old French and American war bunkers at the summit for panoramic views of the South China Sea and lush green mountains.
experiences.location: Hai Van Pass, between Da Nang and Hue

experiences.name: Mekong Delta Day Trip by Boat
experiences.description: Take a budget group boat tour through the winding waterways of the Mekong Delta from Ho Chi Minh City. Visit floating markets, local coconut candy workshops, and rice paper factories. Sample tropical fruits, fresh spring rolls, and sip on coconut water straight from the shell while experiencing authentic rural Vietnamese life.

experiences.name: Bui Vien Walking Street Backpacker Experience
experiences.description: Dive into the heart of Ho Chi Minh City's legendary backpacker district on Bui Vien Street. Enjoy cheap local beers, fresh Vietnamese BBQ skewers, and banh mi from street carts while soaking in the vibrant atmosphere of live music, neon lights, and fellow travelers from around the world. A quintessential budget backpacker rite of passage in Vietnam.
experiences.location: Bui Vien Street, Pham Ngu Lao District, Ho Chi Minh City

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Vietnam
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled - flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Noi Bai International Airport at 13:00. Take the budget-friendly public bus No. 86 or a pre-booked airport shuttle (~50,000-100,000 VND) to the Old Quarter. Check into Boutique Stay in Old Quarter, freshen up, and take a slow orientation walk through the narrow, bustling streets of the 36 Ancient Streets area. Explore Hang Gai, Hang Dao, and Hang Bac streets to get your bearings.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Hoan Kiem Lake for a relaxed evening stroll. Watch locals doing tai chi and socializing around the lake. Cross the iconic red Huc Bridge to visit Ngoc Son Temple (entry ~30,000 VND). End the night by wandering into the Hanoi Night Market on Hang Dao Street, which runs every Friday to Sunday evening.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the plane or grab a quick snack at the airport
meals.lunch: Grab a bowl of Pho Bo (beef noodle soup) from a street stall near the Old Quarter for around 40,000-60,000 VND
meals.dinner: Visit Bun Cha Huong Lien or any local bun cha stall on Hang Manh Street - grilled pork with noodles for ~60,000 VND. Wash it down with a Bia Hoi (fresh draft beer) for just 10,000-15,000 VND at a corner street stall.

day_by_day.notes: Exchange currency at the airport or use ATMs in the Old Quarter (Vietcombank or Techcombank have low fees). Buy a local SIM card at the airport for cheap data (~100,000 VND for 10GB). Keep small bills handy for street food vendors.

day_by_day.morning: Start early with a street-side breakfast, then visit Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum Complex (free entry to the grounds, mausoleum viewing free but check seasonal hours). Walk through Ba Dinh Square and admire the Presidential Palace and Ho Chi Minh's Stilt House (~40,000 VND). Nearby, visit the One Pillar Pagoda, one of Vietnam's most iconic landmarks - entry is free.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Vietnam Museum of Ethnology (~40,000 VND entry) to learn about the country's 54 ethnic groups - a culturally rich and budget-friendly experience. Alternatively, visit the Temple of Literature (Van Mieu), Vietnam's first university, for ~30,000 VND. Walk or take a Grab bike between sites to save money.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Old Quarter and explore the vibrant street food scene on Ta Hien Street, known as 'Beer Street.' Join locals on tiny plastic stools, sip Bia Hoi, and snack on grilled skewers and nem ran (fried spring rolls). Soak in the electric atmosphere of Hanoi's backpacker hub.

meals.breakfast: Banh Mi from a street cart near Hoan Kiem Lake - crispy baguette with pate, veggies, and chili for ~25,000-35,000 VND
meals.lunch: Bun Thang (rice vermicelli with chicken and egg) at a local quan (eatery) near the museum for ~50,000 VND
meals.dinner: Grilled skewers and Bia Hoi on Ta Hien Street - budget around 80,000-120,000 VND for a full evening of snacks and drinks

day_by_day.notes: Dress modestly when visiting the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum complex - no shorts or sleeveless tops. The mausoleum may be closed on Mondays and Fridays for maintenance. Grab bikes (motorbike taxis via app) are the cheapest and fastest way to get around Hanoi - typically 15,000-30,000 VND per short trip.

day_by_day.date: Day 3 - April 17, 2027 (Hanoi Culture & Hoa Lo Prison)
day_by_day.morning: Visit Hoa Lo Prison (Hanoi Hilton) in the morning when it's less crowded. Entry is only ~30,000 VND and it offers a deeply moving look at Vietnamese history during French colonial rule and the American War. Spend 1.5-2 hours exploring the exhibits. Afterward, walk to St. Joseph's Cathedral nearby for a look at stunning French Gothic architecture - free to enter.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a free self-guided walk through the French Quarter, admiring colonial architecture. Visit the Vietnam Fine Arts Museum (~40,000 VND) on Nguyen Thai Hoc Street to explore traditional lacquerware, silk paintings, and folk art. Stop by Dong Xuan Market - Hanoi's largest covered market - for cheap souvenirs, snacks, and a real slice of local life.
day_by_day.evening: Attend the famous Thang Long Water Puppet Theatre show near Hoan Kiem Lake (~100,000 VND for standard seats). This 1,000-year-old art form is a must-see cultural experience. Book tickets in the afternoon to secure your spot. After the show, grab dinner at a nearby pho stall.

meals.breakfast: Xoi Xeo (sticky rice with mung bean and fried shallots) from a street vendor near the hotel - ~20,000-30,000 VND
meals.lunch: Bun Oc (snail noodle soup) at a local eatery near Dong Xuan Market for ~50,000 VND - adventurous and delicious
meals.dinner: Pho Thin on Lo Duc Street - famous for stir-fried beef pho, a Hanoi classic for ~60,000-70,000 VND

day_by_day.notes: Book water puppet theatre tickets early in the day as shows sell out, especially on weekends. The show lasts about 50 minutes and is entirely worth the cost. Dong Xuan Market is a great place to practice bargaining - always start at 50% of the asking price.

day_by_day.date: Day 4 - April 18, 2027 (Day Trip to Ninh Binh)
day_by_day.morning: Take an early morning bus from Hanoi's Giap Bat Bus Station to Ninh Binh (~2.5 hours, ~80,000-100,000 VND). Arrive and rent a bicycle (~50,000-80,000 VND/day) to explore the area. Head to Trang An Landscape Complex - a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Take a 2-3 hour boat tour through stunning limestone karsts and caves (official price: ~250,000 VND per person, negotiate for group boats).
day_by_day.afternoon: Cycle to Hoa Lu Ancient Capital (~20,000 VND entry) to see the ancient temples of the Dinh and Le dynasties set against dramatic karst mountains. Then cycle or take a xe om (motorbike taxi) to the base of Mua Cave (Hang Mua) and climb 500 steps to the dragon statue summit for a breathtaking panoramic view of the rice paddies (~100,000 VND entry).
day_by_day.evening: Head back to Ninh Binh town for dinner before catching the evening bus back to Hanoi (~80,000-100,000 VND). Arrive back in the Old Quarter by 20:00-21:00.

meals.breakfast: Grab Banh Mi or sticky rice from a street stall near the bus station before departure
meals.lunch: Com Rang (fried rice) or Bun Bo Nam Bo at a local restaurant in Ninh Binh town for ~50,000-70,000 VND
meals.dinner: Dê Núi (mountain goat) is Ninh Binh's specialty - try it at a local restaurant for ~80,000-120,000 VND before heading back to Hanoi

day_by_day.notes: Start as early as possible (6:00-7:00 AM bus) to maximize time in Ninh Binh. Bring sunscreen, a hat, and water as the Mua Cave climb can be tiring. This is a very popular day trip - weekdays are less crowded. Total day trip budget: approximately 700,000-900,000 VND including transport, entry fees, and food.

day_by_day.morning: Check out of the Hanoi hotel early. Take a Grab to Hanoi Railway Station and board the morning train to Hue (SE1 or SE3 train, ~6-8 hours, hard seat ~200,000 VND or soft seat ~350,000 VND). The train journey through northern Vietnamese countryside is scenic and a quintessential backpacker experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Hue in the late afternoon. Check into a budget guesthouse or hostel near the city center (dorm beds from ~120,000-150,000 VND/night). Drop your bags and take a walk along the Perfume River (Song Huong) as the sun sets. The riverside promenade is free and beautiful in the golden hour light.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the lively Dong Ba Market area for street food and local atmosphere. Walk along Le Loi Street for budget eateries. Hue is famous for its royal cuisine - try as many local specialties as possible tonight.

meals.breakfast: Quick Banh Mi or pho near Hanoi station before boarding the train
meals.lunch: Pack snacks and instant noodles for the train, or buy food from vendors who walk through the train carriages (~20,000-40,000 VND per item)
meals.dinner: Bun Bo Hue (Hue-style spicy beef noodle soup) at a local quan near Dong Ba Market - the real version is far better than anywhere else in Vietnam, ~50,000-70,000 VND

day_by_day.notes: Book train tickets in advance at the station or via the Vietnam Railways website (dsvn.vn). Soft seats are recommended for the 6-8 hour journey for comfort. Keep your valuables secure on the train. Hue is more relaxed and less touristy than Hanoi or Ho Chi Minh City - enjoy the slower pace.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Imperial Citadel of Hue (Kinh Thanh), the former seat of the Nguyen Dynasty emperors. Entry is ~200,000 VND but covers the entire complex including the Forbidden Purple City. Spend 2-3 hours exploring the ornate palaces, gates, and gardens. Hire a local guide (~100,000-150,000 VND) for deeper historical context.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a bicycle (~50,000-80,000 VND/day) and cycle along the Perfume River to visit the Royal Tombs. The Tomb of Tu Duc is the most atmospheric and photogenic (~100,000 VND entry). Optionally visit the Thien Mu Pagoda (free entry) on the riverbank - a beautiful seven-story tower that is one of Hue's most iconic images.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the city center and explore the night market near Dong Ba Bridge. Sample Hue's unique street foods in a relaxed setting. End the night with a walk across Truong Tien Bridge, beautifully lit up at night.

meals.breakfast: Banh Canh (thick noodle soup) at a local stall near the hostel - a Hue breakfast staple for ~40,000-50,000 VND
meals.lunch: Com Hen (tiny clam rice) near the Imperial Citadel - a uniquely Hue dish for ~30,000-40,000 VND. Try Banh Khoai (crispy Hue pancake) from street stalls for ~20,000-30,000 VND
meals.dinner: Banh Beo, Banh Nam, and Banh Loc (Hue royal rice cakes) at a local restaurant on Nguyen Binh Khiem Street - a set of small dishes for ~60,000-80,000 VND total

day_by_day.notes: Hue's cuisine is distinct from the rest of Vietnam - spicier, more complex, and influenced by royal court cooking. Don't miss the opportunity to try as many local specialties as possible. The Imperial Citadel is large - wear comfortable shoes. Cycling is the best way to see the royal tombs spread along the river.

day_by_day.date: Day 7 - April 21, 2027 (Hai Van Pass & Travel to Hoi An)
day_by_day.morning: Hire a motorbike taxi or join a budget group tour to travel from Hue to Hoi An via the legendary Hai Van Pass (~150,000-200,000 VND for xe om, or ~250,000-350,000 VND for a group tour including stops). The Hai Van Pass is one of the most scenic coastal mountain passes in Southeast Asia. Stop at the old French and American War bunkers at the summit for panoramic views of Da Nang Bay.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue down to Da Nang briefly, then push on to Hoi An Ancient Town. Check into a budget hostel in or near the Ancient Town (dorms from ~120,000-150,000 VND). Drop your bags and take your first walk through the UNESCO-listed Ancient Town's yellow-walled lanes, Japanese Covered Bridge, and Chinese Assembly Halls.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Hoi An Ancient Town at night when it is at its most magical - lanterns glow everywhere and the Thu Bon River reflects the colorful lights. Buy a floating lantern (~20,000-30,000 VND) and release it on the river for good luck. Stroll the pedestrian-only streets and browse the night market.

meals.breakfast: Eat before departure from the hostel or grab a quick Banh Mi in Hue
meals.lunch: Stop at a roadside restaurant during the Hai Van Pass journey for Com Phan (set rice meal) for ~50,000-70,000 VND
meals.dinner: Cao Lau (Hoi An's signature thick noodle dish with pork and greens) at Thanh Cao Lau or a local stall in the Ancient Town for ~50,000-70,000 VND

day_by_day.notes: The Hai Van Pass motorbike journey is iconic but can be cold and windy at the summit - bring a light jacket. The bus through the tunnel is cheaper (~50,000 VND) but you miss the stunning scenery entirely. If budget is very tight, take the open-tour bus from Hue to Hoi An (~150,000-200,000 VND) which stops at the pass.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Hoi An Ancient Town in the morning before the crowds arrive. Visit the Japanese Covered Bridge (Chua Cau) - entry included in the Ancient Town ticket (~120,000 VND covers 5 sites). See the Tan Ky Old House, Phuc Kien Assembly Hall, and stroll through the covered market. Take a free self-guided walking tour using an offline map.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a bicycle (~50,000-80,000 VND/day) and cycle 4km to An Bang Beach or Cua Dai Beach for a relaxing afternoon by the sea. The ride through rice paddies and villages is beautiful. Alternatively, take a cooking class - budget cooking classes in Hoi An start from ~300,000-400,000 VND and include a market visit, which is excellent value.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Ancient Town for the evening lantern atmosphere. Visit the Hoi An Night Market on An Hoi Islet (cross the small footbridge). Browse handmade lanterns, try local snacks, and watch traditional music performances that sometimes happen along the riverside. Very budget-friendly evening.

meals.breakfast: Banh Mi Phuong (famous Hoi An banh mi) on Phan Chau Trinh Street - consistently ranked one of the best banh mi in Vietnam for ~35,000-45,000 VND
meals.lunch: White Rose Dumplings (Banh Vac) and Fried Wontons at a local restaurant in the Ancient Town - ~50,000-70,000 VND for a combination plate
meals.dinner: Com Ga Hoi An (Hoi An chicken rice) at Ba Buoi restaurant or similar local spot for ~50,000-60,000 VND - a simple, delicious local staple

day_by_day.notes: The Ancient Town entry ticket (~120,000 VND) covers 5 specific sites and is valid for one day. Entry to the town itself is free - you only pay when entering ticketed sites. Hoi An is very walkable and bicycle-friendly. Avoid the overpriced tourist restaurants on the main streets - duck into the side alleys for authentic, cheaper food.

day_by_day.date: Day 9 - April 23, 2027 (Travel to Ho Chi Minh City / Saigon)
day_by_day.morning: Check out of the hostel and take a local bus or Grab to Da Nang Airport (about 30km, ~100,000-150,000 VND by Grab). Catch a budget domestic flight to Ho Chi Minh City (Tan Son Nhat Airport) - book in advance with VietJet Air or Bamboo Airways for as low as 300,000-600,000 VND. Alternatively, take an overnight bus from Hoi An (~200,000-250,000 VND) to save on accommodation.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Ho Chi Minh City. Take the public bus No. 152 from the airport to the city center (~6,000 VND - incredibly cheap!) or a Grab (~80,000-120,000 VND). Check into a budget hostel in District 1 or the Pham Ngu Lao backpacker area (dorms from ~120,000-150,000 VND). Get oriented with a walk through the Pham Ngu Lao area.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Ben Thanh Market area as it transitions into the night market. Walk along Nguyen Hue Walking Street and see the iconic Ho Chi Minh City Hall (illuminated at night). Visit the Bitexco Financial Tower for city views (observation deck ~200,000 VND) or save money by admiring the skyline from street level.

meals.breakfast: Grab a quick Banh Mi or Xoi from a street stall near the Hoi An hostel before departure
meals.lunch: Airport food or a quick meal near the hostel upon arrival in HCMC - look for Com Binh Dan (workers' rice) restaurants for a full meal for ~40,000-60,000 VND
meals.dinner: Banh Xeo (sizzling Vietnamese crepe) at a local restaurant in District 1 for ~60,000-80,000 VND, or explore the Pham Ngu Lao street food stalls

day_by_day.notes: Book domestic flights well in advance for the best budget prices. The public bus from the airport is the cheapest option but takes longer. The Pham Ngu Lao area (District 1) is the classic backpacker hub with the most affordable hostels, restaurants, and travel agencies. Ho Chi Minh City traffic is intense - be very careful when crossing streets.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the War Remnants Museum (~40,000 VND) - one of the most powerful and important museums in Southeast Asia, documenting the Vietnam War from the Vietnamese perspective. Allow 2 hours. Nearby, see the Reunification Palace (Independence Palace, ~40,000 VND entry) where the Vietnam War officially ended on April 30, 1975.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Notre-Dame Cathedral Basilica of Saigon (free, exterior viewing) and the historic Central Post Office designed by Gustave Eiffel - free to enter and still functioning. Explore the Ben Thanh Market for last-minute souvenir shopping (bargain hard!). Take a Grab to District 4 or District 8 to experience a more local, less touristy side of the city.
day_by_day.evening: Spend your final evening on Bui Vien Walking Street - the famous backpacker street of Ho Chi Minh City, buzzing with energy, live music, street food, and travelers from around the world. Reflect on the incredible 10-day journey over a final Bia Saigon (Saigon beer) and a bowl of noodles. Celebrate your budget Vietnam adventure!

meals.breakfast: Pho or Hu Tieu (Southern-style noodle soup) at a local pho shop near the hostel for ~50,000-60,000 VND - a classic Saigon morning
meals.lunch: Banh Mi from a street cart (Saigon style has more fillings than the North) for ~25,000-40,000 VND, or Com Tam (broken rice with grilled pork) - the quintessential Saigon dish for ~50,000-70,000 VND
meals.dinner: Farewell feast on Bui Vien Street - grilled seafood skewers, fresh spring rolls, and Bia Saigon. Budget ~100,000-150,000 VND for a satisfying final meal with drinks

day_by_day.notes: The War Remnants Museum is emotionally intense - take your time and be respectful. Ho Chi Minh City is much hotter and more frenetic than Hanoi - stay hydrated. If departing by flight, allow at least 3 hours before departure for the journey to the airport and check-in. Tan Son Nhat Airport is about 7-10km from District 1. Total estimated 10-day budget (excluding flights): approximately 3,500,000-5,000,000 VND (~$140-200 USD) for a true budget backpacker experience.

trip_options.title: Classic Vietnam Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Hanoi Noi Bai International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Take a taxi or airport bus (Bus 86) to the Old Quarter hotel. Check in, freshen up, and rest after the flight.
day_by_day.afternoon: Gentle orientation walk around the Old Quarter. Stroll the 36 ancient streets (Hang Gai, Hang Bac, Hang Dao), browse silk and lacquerware shops, and visit Hoan Kiem Lake and the iconic red Huc Bridge to Ngoc Son Temple.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Hanoi Night Market on Hang Dao Street (open Fri–Sun; if a weekday, wander Ta Hien Beer Street instead). Soak up the buzzing atmosphere, sample street snacks, and settle into the city rhythm.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in transit
meals.lunch: Grab a quick Banh Mi from a street cart near the airport or Old Quarter upon arrival (~30,000–40,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Bun Cha Huong Lien (famous spot on Le Van Huu) — grilled pork with rice noodles, ~80,000 VND per person

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light. Exchange currency at a reputable bank or ATM in the Old Quarter. Avoid jet lag by staying awake until local bedtime. April in Hanoi is warm (~28°C) with occasional light showers — pack a light rain jacket.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum complex (open mornings only, closed Mon/Fri). See the Presidential Palace, Ho Chi Minh's Stilt House, and the One Pillar Pagoda. Arrive early to beat crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Temple of Literature (Van Mieu) — Vietnam's first university, a beautifully preserved Confucian temple complex. Then visit the Vietnam Museum of Ethnology nearby to understand the country's 54 ethnic groups.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a Traditional Water Puppet Show at Thang Long Water Puppet Theatre in the Old Quarter (~100,000 VND). A uniquely Vietnamese art form not to be missed.

meals.breakfast: Pho Bo (beef pho) at Pho Gia Truyen on Bat Dan Street — a Hanoi institution (~60,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Bun Rieu (crab noodle soup) at a local stall near the Temple of Literature (~50,000–70,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Cha Ca La Vong on Cha Ca Street — turmeric-marinated fish with dill, a Hanoi specialty (~150,000–200,000 VND)

day_by_day.notes: Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum requires modest dress (covered shoulders and knees). Book water puppet tickets in advance during peak season. The Museum of Ethnology is worth 2 hours and has excellent English signage.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Ninh Binh (2 hours by bus or train from Hanoi). Rent a bicycle at Tam Coc and cycle through stunning karst limestone scenery and rice paddies.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a 2-hour rowboat tour through the Tam Coc caves along the Ngo Dong River — often called 'Ha Long Bay on land.' Then visit Bich Dong Pagoda, a cave pagoda carved into the cliff face.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Hanoi by early evening. Relax with a Bia Hoi (fresh draft beer, ~10,000 VND) at a plastic-stool street corner bar on Ta Hien Street.

meals.breakfast: Xoi (sticky rice with toppings) from a street vendor in the Old Quarter (~30,000–40,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Com Rang (fried rice with vegetables and egg) at a local restaurant in Tam Coc village (~60,000–80,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Bun Oc (snail noodle soup) at a street stall in the Old Quarter (~50,000–70,000 VND)

day_by_day.notes: Book a bus or train to Ninh Binh the day before. Bicycle rental in Tam Coc costs ~50,000 VND/day. Rowboat tours cost ~150,000 VND. Wear sunscreen — the open rice fields offer little shade. Return bus to Hanoi departs Ninh Binh around 16:00–17:00.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Hanoi by sleeper train or flight to Da Nang (train ~16 hours overnight option, or budget flight ~1.5 hours). If flying, take the morning flight and arrive by midday. Check into a mid-range guesthouse in Da Nang or Hoi An.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head directly to Hoi An Ancient Town (30 min from Da Nang by taxi/bus). Walk the lantern-lit streets of the UNESCO World Heritage Site. Visit the iconic Japanese Covered Bridge and Phung Hung Old House.
day_by_day.evening: Wander Hoi An's night market along the Thu Bon River. Browse handmade lanterns, silk goods, and local crafts. Watch lanterns float on the river — especially magical near the full moon.

meals.breakfast: Banh Mi Phuong in Hoi An (if arriving early enough) or grab food at Hanoi airport (~50,000–80,000 VND)
meals.lunch: White Rose Dumplings (Banh Bao Vac) at White Rose Restaurant in Hoi An — a local specialty (~80,000–100,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Cao Lau (Hoi An's signature thick noodle dish) at Thanh Cao Lau restaurant (~70,000–90,000 VND)

day_by_day.notes: Book flights or train in advance. Budget airlines like VietJet and Bamboo Airways offer Da Nang flights from ~500,000–800,000 VND. Hoi An Ancient Town charges a 120,000 VND entrance ticket that includes 5 heritage site visits. Stay in Hoi An for a more atmospheric experience.

day_by_day.morning: Rent a bicycle (~50,000 VND/day) and cycle to the My Son Sanctuary — ancient Cham Hindu temple ruins set in a jungle valley, a UNESCO World Heritage Site (~150,000 VND entry). Explore the moss-covered towers and learn about the Champa Kingdom.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Hoi An and visit the Tra Que Vegetable Village on the outskirts. Join a hands-on cooking class (2–3 hours, ~300,000–500,000 VND) — learn to make Hoi An specialties using fresh herbs grown in the village.
day_by_day.evening: Take a lantern-making workshop in the Old Quarter (~150,000–200,000 VND) or simply enjoy a sunset drink at a riverside cafe along the Thu Bon River.

meals.breakfast: Banh Mi from Banh Mi Phuong — arguably Vietnam's best banh mi (~35,000–45,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Com Ga (chicken rice) at Com Ga Ba Buoi in Hoi An — a beloved local staple (~60,000–80,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Fresh seafood BBQ at a riverside restaurant in Hoi An (~150,000–250,000 VND per person)

day_by_day.notes: My Son is best visited early morning before the heat peaks. Hire a guide at the site for deeper historical context (~100,000 VND). The cooking class typically includes a market visit — a wonderful cultural experience.

day_by_day.morning: Visit An Bang Beach or Cua Dai Beach (5–7 km from Hoi An by bicycle). Swim, relax, and enjoy the quieter stretches of coastline before the day heats up.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Da Nang and visit the Marble Mountains (Ngu Hanh Son) — a cluster of five marble and limestone hills with caves, tunnels, and Buddhist sanctuaries (~40,000 VND entry). Climb to the top for panoramic views.
day_by_day.evening: Walk across the famous Dragon Bridge in Da Nang and explore the Han Market for local produce, textiles, and souvenirs. On weekends, stay until 21:00 to watch the Dragon Bridge breathe fire.

meals.breakfast: Mi Quang (turmeric noodles with pork and shrimp) at a local Da Nang stall (~50,000–70,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood lunch at a beachside shack near An Bang Beach (~100,000–150,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Banh Xeo (Vietnamese sizzling crepes) at a street restaurant near Han Market (~80,000–120,000 VND)

day_by_day.notes: Dragon Bridge fire show is every Saturday and Sunday at 21:00. Marble Mountains can be hot in the afternoon — wear comfortable shoes for climbing. Consider a quick stop at the Da Nang Museum of Cham Sculpture if time allows (~60,000 VND).

day_by_day.morning: Take a morning flight or sleeper train from Da Nang to Ho Chi Minh City (HCMC / Saigon). Flight is ~1.5 hours. Check into a mid-range guesthouse in District 1 or the Pham Ngu Lao backpacker area.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the War Remnants Museum (~40,000 VND) — a powerful and sobering look at the Vietnam War through Vietnamese eyes. Then walk to the Reunification Palace (~40,000 VND) to explore the historic government complex.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Ben Thanh Night Market and surrounding street food stalls. Walk along Nguyen Hue Walking Street and admire the HCMC City Hall lit up at night.

meals.breakfast: Airport food or grab a Banh Mi on arrival in HCMC (~40,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Com Tam (broken rice with grilled pork) at Com Tam Moc on Hoang Dieu Street — an HCMC staple (~70,000–90,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Hu Tieu Nam Vang (Cambodian-style noodle soup) at a street stall near Pham Ngu Lao (~60,000–80,000 VND)

day_by_day.notes: Book morning flights to maximize afternoon time in HCMC. The War Remnants Museum is emotionally intense — allocate 1.5–2 hours. HCMC traffic is intense; use Grab (ride-hailing app) for affordable and convenient transport throughout the city.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the Cu Chi Tunnels (~40 km northwest of HCMC). Join a half-day guided tour (~300,000–500,000 VND including transport). Crawl through the narrow guerrilla tunnels used during the Vietnam War — a fascinating and unique experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to HCMC and visit the Jade Emperor Pagoda (Phuoc Hai Tu) — a stunning Taoist temple filled with intricate carvings and incense smoke. Then explore the lively Chinatown district (Cho Lon) and Binh Tay Market.
day_by_day.evening: Take a street food tour on foot or by motorbike through District 1 and District 3. Sample Banh Trang Nuong (grilled rice paper), Goi Cuon (fresh spring rolls), and local desserts like Che.

meals.breakfast: Banh Cuon (steamed rice rolls) at a local breakfast spot in District 1 (~50,000–70,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Lunch included in Cu Chi tour or eat at a local restaurant near the tunnels (~80,000–100,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Lau (Vietnamese hot pot) at a local restaurant in District 3 — great for a social evening (~150,000–200,000 VND per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book Cu Chi Tunnels tour through your guesthouse or a reputable agency. Wear old clothes — the tunnels are dusty. Ben Duoc site is less touristy than Ben Dinh. The motorbike street food tour is a highlight — book through Airbnb Experiences or local operators (~400,000–600,000 VND).

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the Mekong Delta. Take a guided tour to My Tho or Ben Tre (~150 km from HCMC). Board a wooden boat through narrow waterways, visit floating markets, coconut candy workshops, and local fruit orchards.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Mekong experience — cycle through riverside villages, watch traditional rice paper or rice wine production, and enjoy a homestay-style lunch with a local family.
day_by_day.evening: Return to HCMC by early evening. Visit the Saigon Skydeck at Bitexco Financial Tower for panoramic city views at sunset (~200,000 VND) or enjoy rooftop drinks at a bar in District 1.

meals.breakfast: Xoi Man (savory sticky rice) from a street cart near your guesthouse (~35,000–50,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Traditional Mekong lunch included in most tours — elephant ear fish (Ca Loc), fresh spring rolls, and tropical fruits (~included or ~100,000 VND supplement)
meals.dinner: Pho Saigon (southern-style beef pho) at a local pho shop in District 1 (~70,000–90,000 VND)

day_by_day.notes: Book a Mekong Delta day tour through your guesthouse or a reputable operator (~400,000–700,000 VND). Opt for a smaller group tour for a more authentic experience. The Cai Rang floating market near Can Tho is more impressive but requires an overnight stay.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in HCMC. Visit the Notre-Dame Cathedral Basilica of Saigon and the nearby Central Post Office — a beautiful French colonial building designed by Gustave Eiffel. Browse the Dong Khoi Street area for last-minute souvenirs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the HCMC Museum (~30,000 VND) for a comprehensive overview of the city's history, or relax at a rooftop cafe. Do final souvenir shopping at Ben Thanh Market — practice bargaining! Pack and prepare for departure.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at a mid-range Vietnamese restaurant. Depart for Tan Son Nhat International Airport (allow 1.5–2 hours before flight due to HCMC traffic). End of an unforgettable 10-day Vietnam journey.

meals.breakfast: Full Vietnamese breakfast spread at your guesthouse or a nearby cafe — Pho, Banh Mi, and Vietnamese iced coffee (Ca Phe Sua Da) (~60,000–80,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Goi Cuon and Banh Khot (mini savory pancakes) at a local restaurant in District 1 (~80,000–120,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Nha Hang Ngon on Nam Ky Khoi Nghia — a beautiful courtyard restaurant serving dishes from all regions of Vietnam (~150,000–250,000 VND per person)

day_by_day.notes: Allow ample time to reach the airport — HCMC traffic can be severe, especially in the evening. Use Grab for a reliable fare estimate. Confirm your flight details and check-in online. Keep some VND for airport snacks. Reflect on 10 incredible days across Vietnam's north, center, and south!

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Vietnam Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Noi Bai International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private luxury transfer arranged from airport to Boutique Stay in Old Quarter, Hanoi (approx. 45 min ride in a premium vehicle with complimentary welcome drinks and cold towels).
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to the boutique hotel and freshen up. Take a leisurely orientation stroll through the iconic 36 Streets of the Old Quarter — explore Hang Gai (Silk Street), Hang Bac (Silver Street), and the vibrant alleyways. Visit Ngoc Son Temple on Hoan Kiem Lake for a serene cultural introduction to Hanoi.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at a rooftop bar overlooking Hoan Kiem Lake (Cà phê Trứng — egg coffee — is a must-try Hanoi specialty). Dinner at a premium Old Quarter restaurant to ease into Vietnamese cuisine.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in-flight meal
meals.lunch: Light welcome snack at hotel upon arrival or a quick stop at Banh Mi 25 (renowned street-food stall, Old Quarter) for a premium bánh mì
meals.dinner: Dinner at Chả Cá Thăng Long — a legendary Hanoi institution famous for turmeric-marinated grilled fish (chả cá) served tableside with dill and vermicelli

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 begins post-arrival. Keep the schedule light to recover from the flight. Confirm hotel concierge for next-day private guides and experiences. April in Hanoi is warm (26–32°C) with occasional light showers — pack a light layer.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning visit to Hoan Kiem Lake for the authentic local experience — watch elderly locals practice Tai Chi by the lakeside at dawn. Walk to St. Joseph's Cathedral (Hanoi's Gothic-style landmark) and explore the surrounding boutique coffee scene. Visit the Temple of Literature (Van Mieu) — Vietnam's first national university, a stunning 11th-century Confucian complex.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Vietnam Museum of Ethnology — one of Southeast Asia's finest cultural museums, showcasing 54 ethnic groups with immersive outdoor exhibits. Private guided tour recommended for deep cultural context. Return to the Old Quarter for a curated street food walking tour with a premium local guide.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a Traditional Water Puppet Show at Thang Long Water Puppet Theatre — a uniquely Vietnamese art form dating back to the 11th century. Post-show dinner at a fine-dining Vietnamese restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Phở Thìn (49 Dinh Tien Hoang) — Hanoi's most celebrated phở bò (beef noodle soup) restaurant, a street-food legend
meals.lunch: Bún Chả Hương Liên (made famous by Anthony Bourdain and Barack Obama) — grilled pork with vermicelli noodles and dipping broth
meals.dinner: Dinner at Green Tangerine Restaurant — elegant French-Vietnamese fusion cuisine in a beautifully restored 1928 colonial villa in the Old Quarter

day_by_day.notes: Book Water Puppet Show tickets in advance through hotel concierge. The Museum of Ethnology is best visited with a private English-speaking guide for maximum cultural immersion.

day_by_day.morning: Private day trip to Ninh Binh (2 hours from Hanoi) — known as 'Ha Long Bay on land.' Boat tour through the stunning karst limestone landscape of Tam Coc via traditional hand-rowed bamboo boats along the Ngo Dong River. Pass through emerald rice paddies and cave tunnels.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Bich Dong Pagoda — a 15th-century cave pagoda carved into a limestone mountain. Cycle through the scenic Tam Coc countryside on private e-bikes or traditional bicycles. Explore Hoa Lu Ancient Capital — the 10th-century imperial citadel of the Dinh and Le dynasties.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Hanoi by private vehicle. Evening at leisure — explore the Old Quarter Night Market (open Friday–Sunday) or enjoy a premium spa treatment at the hotel. Dinner in the Old Quarter.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or Xôi Yến (35 Nguyen Huu Huan) — premium sticky rice dishes, a beloved Hanoi morning staple
meals.lunch: Traditional set lunch at a riverside restaurant in Ninh Binh — fresh mountain goat (dê núi) and local rice wine are regional specialties
meals.dinner: Madame Hien Restaurant (Hanoi) — refined Vietnamese cuisine in a stunning 1930s colonial townhouse, celebrating traditional recipes with premium ingredients

day_by_day.notes: Ninh Binh day trip is approximately 10–11 hours total. Wear comfortable walking shoes and bring sun protection. Private vehicle and guide highly recommended for a seamless premium experience.

day_by_day.morning: Private flight or premium sleeper train from Hanoi to Hue (flight recommended for luxury travel — approx. 1 hour). Check in to a luxury heritage hotel in Hue (e.g., Azerai La Residence Hue or Pilgrimage Village Boutique Resort). Morning visit to the Imperial Citadel of Hue — the UNESCO-listed seat of the Nguyen Dynasty, a vast walled complex with palaces, temples, and moats.
day_by_day.afternoon: Dragon Boat cruise along the Perfume River to Thien Mu Pagoda — Hue's most iconic seven-tiered pagoda perched on a hillside. Visit the elaborate Royal Tomb of Minh Mang — the most architecturally refined of all Nguyen emperor tombs, set within serene forested grounds.
day_by_day.evening: Royal Hue cuisine dinner experience — Hue is considered the culinary capital of Vietnam, famous for its elaborate imperial court cuisine. Enjoy a private royal banquet-style dinner.

meals.breakfast: In-flight snack or hotel welcome breakfast upon arrival
meals.lunch: Lunch at Lac Thien or Lac Thanh Restaurant — legendary Hue establishments famous for bánh khoái (crispy rice crepes) and nem lụi (lemongrass skewers)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Tịnh Gia Viên — a meticulously restored 19th-century aristocratic garden house offering an authentic imperial Hue multi-course tasting menu

day_by_day.notes: Hue's imperial sites are extensive — comfortable footwear is essential. Book royal dinner experiences in advance. The Perfume River boat cruise is best enjoyed in late afternoon light.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Tomb of Tu Duc — the most poetic and romantically designed royal tomb, surrounded by lotus ponds and pine forests. Explore Dong Ba Market — Hue's largest and most vibrant traditional market, a sensory feast of local produce, spices, and street snacks. Take a premium cooking class at a local culinary school to learn Hue's signature dishes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive the legendary Hai Van Pass (Cloud Pass) — one of the world's most scenic coastal mountain roads, offering dramatic views of Da Nang Bay. Stop at the French-era bunkers at the summit. Descend into Da Nang and check in to a luxury beachfront resort (e.g., InterContinental Danang Sun Peninsula Resort or Hyatt Regency Danang).
day_by_day.evening: Sunset walk along My Khe Beach — one of Forbes' most beautiful beaches in Asia. Evening exploration of Da Nang's illuminated Dragon Bridge (fire-breathing show on weekends). Dinner at a premium Da Nang seafood restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — sample bún bò Huế (spicy Hue-style beef noodle soup), considered by many chefs as Vietnam's greatest noodle dish
meals.lunch: Roadside lunch stop at a local restaurant on the Hai Van Pass route — fresh seafood with views of the coastline
meals.dinner: Dinner at Waterfront Restaurant Da Nang — contemporary Vietnamese and international cuisine with panoramic Han River views

day_by_day.notes: The Hue to Da Nang leg via Hai Van Pass is best done by private car (approx. 2.5 hours). This is one of Vietnam's most spectacular drives — allocate ample time for photo stops.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Hoi An Ancient Town (30 min from Da Nang) — a UNESCO World Heritage Site and one of Southeast Asia's best-preserved trading ports. Morning walking tour of the lantern-lit old town: visit the iconic Japanese Covered Bridge (1593), Phuc Kien Assembly Hall, and traditional merchant houses. Commission a bespoke tailored garment at one of Hoi An's renowned custom tailors.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Hoi An's vibrant Central Market and riverside food stalls. Cycle through the lush rice paddies and water buffalo fields of the surrounding countryside on a premium guided cycling tour. Visit the Tra Que Vegetable Village — a serene organic farming community where you can participate in traditional farming activities.
day_by_day.evening: Hoi An at dusk is magical — the Ancient Town glows with hundreds of silk lanterns. Join a premium lantern-making workshop. Dinner at one of Hoi An's finest restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or Bánh Mì Phượng (Hoi An) — declared by Anthony Bourdain as 'the best bánh mì in the world'
meals.lunch: Cao Lầu at Thanh Cao Lau Restaurant — Hoi An's signature noodle dish made with water from an ancient Cham well, available only in Hoi An
meals.dinner: Dinner at The Field Restaurant Hoi An — farm-to-table Vietnamese cuisine in a stunning open-air setting surrounded by rice paddies and lotus ponds

day_by_day.notes: Hoi An's old town is best explored on foot or by bicycle. Many streets are pedestrian-only. Tailor orders typically require 24–48 hours — place orders early in the day.

day_by_day.morning: Morning at leisure in Da Nang — enjoy the luxury resort's beach club, spa, or infinity pool. Optional: visit the Marble Mountains (Ngu Hanh Son) — a cluster of five limestone and marble hills with caves, tunnels, and Buddhist sanctuaries. Spectacular panoramic views from the summit.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private flight from Da Nang to Ho Chi Minh City (approx. 1 hour). Check in to a luxury hotel in District 1 (e.g., Park Hyatt Saigon, Sofitel Saigon Plaza, or The Reverie Saigon). Afternoon orientation walk through the French colonial heart of Ho Chi Minh City — Notre-Dame Cathedral Basilica, Central Post Office (designed by Gustave Eiffel), and the grand Opera House.
day_by_day.evening: Rooftop cocktails at a sky bar overlooking the glittering Saigon skyline. Dinner at a celebrated Saigon fine-dining restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Luxury resort breakfast with fresh tropical fruit, Vietnamese coffee, and made-to-order dishes
meals.lunch: Light lunch at Da Nang airport lounge or in-flight
meals.dinner: Dinner at Noir. Dining in the Dark — a unique Saigon dining experience where guests eat in complete darkness, heightening all senses, guided by visually impaired staff. Menu features premium Vietnamese cuisine

day_by_day.notes: Book Noir restaurant well in advance — it is one of Saigon's most sought-after dining experiences. The French colonial district is walkable from most District 1 luxury hotels.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the War Remnants Museum — one of Southeast Asia's most powerful and thought-provoking museums, offering essential historical context for understanding modern Vietnam. Explore the Reunification Palace (Independence Palace) — the historic seat of South Vietnam's government, preserved exactly as it was on April 30, 1975.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private day trip to the Cu Chi Tunnels (1.5 hours from Saigon) — the legendary 250km underground tunnel network used by Viet Cong fighters during the Vietnam War. Take a premium 'VIP tunnel' experience with a private expert guide for a more in-depth, less crowded visit.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Saigon. Explore the vibrant Ben Thanh Street Food Market for an authentic Saigon street food evening. Premium cyclo (pedicab) tour through District 1's illuminated colonial streets.

meals.breakfast: Hủ Tiếu Nam Vang at a traditional Saigon breakfast spot — Phnom Penh-style noodle soup, a beloved Saigon morning ritual
meals.lunch: Lunch at a riverside restaurant near Cu Chi — fresh Mekong Delta fish and southern Vietnamese specialties
meals.dinner: Dinner at Cục Gạch Quán — a beloved Saigon institution serving rustic, home-style Vietnamese cuisine in a beautifully converted old villa garden

day_by_day.notes: The Cu Chi Tunnels experience is emotionally and physically engaging — wear comfortable clothes and closed-toe shoes. The VIP tunnel section is wider and more accessible than the standard tourist tunnels.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day premium Mekong Delta cruise departing from Saigon. Board a private luxury speedboat to My Tho, then transfer to a traditional wooden sampan for an immersive journey through narrow waterways, floating markets, and lush tropical islands. Visit a bee farm, coconut candy workshop, and a local fruit orchard.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Mekong Delta exploration — visit a traditional rice paper and coconut wine production village. Lunch on board or at a premium riverside restaurant. Optional: kayak through the mangrove forests of the delta for a more adventurous perspective.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Saigon by private vehicle. Final evening in Ho Chi Minh City — explore the upscale Thao Dien neighborhood (District 2) or the chic Bui Vien Street area. Farewell cocktails at The Reverie Saigon's rooftop bar.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — try Bánh Mì Saigon style with premium fillings from the hotel's Vietnamese breakfast spread
meals.lunch: Premium set lunch at a floating restaurant on the Mekong River — fresh elephant ear fish (cá tai tượng), spring rolls wrapped in rice paper, and local tropical fruits
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Quince Saigon — contemporary European-Vietnamese cuisine with an exceptional wine list, located in a stunning colonial villa in District 2

day_by_day.notes: The Mekong Delta day trip is approximately 10–11 hours. Private boat charter is strongly recommended for a premium experience. Book well in advance through your hotel concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Ho Chi Minh City — leisurely breakfast at the hotel. Last-minute premium shopping at Dong Khoi Street (Saigon's luxury shopping boulevard) for Vietnamese lacquerware, silk, artisan coffee, and designer souvenirs. Visit the Saigon Central Post Office one final time for postcards and premium Vietnamese coffee to bring home.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out from hotel. Private luxury transfer to Tan Son Nhat International Airport. Enjoy the premium airport lounge before departure.
day_by_day.evening: Departure flight. Reflect on 10 extraordinary days experiencing Vietnam's culture, cuisine, history, and natural beauty.

meals.breakfast: Grand hotel breakfast — indulge in a full spread of Vietnamese and international dishes: phở, bánh cuốn (steamed rice rolls), tropical fruits, and Vietnamese egg coffee
meals.lunch: Final Vietnamese lunch at Propaganda Bistro (District 1) — vibrant, design-forward Vietnamese street food elevated to bistro quality, perfect for a memorable last meal
meals.dinner: Airport lounge dining or in-flight meal

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before international departure for check-in and security at Tan Son Nhat Airport. Consider purchasing premium Vietnamese Arabica coffee (Da Lat region), Phu Quoc fish sauce, and artisan lacquerware as luxury souvenirs. Vietnam visa and entry requirements should be confirmed well before travel in April 2027.
